flagged.evidence: The proof says, “In a local oriented coordinate frame,” but does not construct such a frame from the supplied orientation. The orientation definition gives a smooth orientation ray and defines an oriented chart by its coordinate frame lying in that ray; the proof must explain that an arbitrary chart can be adjusted by reversing one coordinate and then restricted to keep the sign fixed.

After noting that $Ae_0$ is future timelike, the proof concludes that “$A$ preserves the selected future component.” The cited cone result gives the two components, but the proof omits that an invertible Lorentz map is a homeomorphism of the timelike set and therefore maps each component to a component; this makes the conclusion follow from the image of $e_0$.

The proof asserts that the inverse-chart matrix entries are smooth because they are obtained from “the smooth frame vectors of $u$,” then later says in Proof 4.1 that the charts define the smooth structure. The frame-bundle supplier provides a topological frame bundle, and the smooth-principal-bundle definition requires a smooth total space. The proof needs to define the atlas using these local maps and establish chart compatibility before using smoothness of coordinates on $P^+_g(M)$.

The path uses $R_t=\begin{pmatrix}r^t&tz\\0&r^{-t}\end{pmatrix}$ for $r>0$, but gives no continuity justification for its entries as functions of $t$. The elementary identity $r^t=\exp(t\log r)$ supplies the needed continuity.

The path $t\mapsto B(tu)$ is asserted continuous although its entries use $\sqrt{1+t^2|u|^2}$ without a continuity justification. The proof also concludes from $B(tu)e_0$ being future timelike that the Lorentz map preserves the future component; this needs the short observation that an invertible Lorentz map is a homeomorphism of the timelike set and hence maps components to components.

The proof says that in the chosen basis $R_3$ is the displayed rotation, then interpolates its angle to obtain a path ending at the original $R_3$ without conjugating that path back to the original coordinates. It also states that a nonreal conjugate eigenvalue pair has product $1$ without spelling out that orthogonality forces its eigenvalues to have modulus one.

The derivative is defined as $[u,df_u(\widetilde X^H_u)]$ for $u\in\widetilde P_x$, without establishing independence of the representative. Replacing $u$ by $ua$ requires using right invariance of the horizontal lift and differentiating $f(ua)=\sigma(a)^{-1}f(u)$; the associated-bundle relation then gives the same class.

The text says, “With the defining representation on $\mathbb C^2$ chosen for spinor components,” but never specifies that representation's action, such as $\sigma(a)v=av$ for $a\in SL(2,\mathbb C)$ and column vector $v\in\mathbb C^2$. The preceding definition allows any smooth representation, so the spinor representation and resulting spinor-bundle terminology remain underspecified.

The Statement says “a $\mathrm{Spin}(4)\to SO(4)$ construction” cannot lift the boost, but neither $\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ nor this map is defined in the item or its dependency list. The only set definition of $SO(4)$ appears later in Facts & Assumptions, after its use in the Statement. The comparison group and map must be defined before use, or omitted.

The Statement asserts a uniqueness claim for “the Cartesian Minkowski tetrad,” and Verification 3.1 uses $e^I=dx^I$, but the item supplies no underlying manifold, coordinates, metric, or tetrad. Its Facts & Assumptions give only the quadratic forms and boost parameter; the sibling example is not a dependency. The claim needs data such as $M=\mathbb R^4$, standard coordinates, $g=\eta$, and $e^I=dx^I$.
